coordinates.note: Surface-projected position of the Davis Cavern detector hall, given by SURF for the LUX detector; LZ occupies the same cavern. Table 5 is headed "Coordinates estimates", so precision_m is set to 50 m rather than the arc-second resolution of the figures. The PDF text lists the table column by column: the first value in each column (599527, 4911873, 44 21 11.88 N, 103 45 04.27 W) belongs to the first row, LUX Detector; the other two rows are MJD Detector and Entrance Cutout. The rank-10 proceedings is the only source found that publishes coordinates; the official SURF Davis Campus page is co-cited for the location itself.

depth_rock.note: 4850 ft below the surface. The SURF science director quotes 1490 m and 1485 m in arXiv:2403.13671; the LZ collaboration value is used here.
depth_rock.quote: in the same cavern as LZ (vertical depth of about 1480 m)

muon_flux.note: Flux through the surface of a sphere of unit cross-sectional area (unit detection efficiency at all angles), derived from the muon rate through LZ (10.94 ± 0.17 per day with energy thresholds of 20 MeV in the xenon TPC and 8 MeV in the outer detector, 366.4 days) and extrapolated to the top of the Davis Cavern, where the paper finds it 3% lower than 7 m into the rock (5.25 ± 0.09 ± 0.10). The Majorana Demonstrator veto measured a total flux of (5.31 ± 0.17) × 10^-9 cm^-2 s^-1 in a nearby cavern at the same level (Abgrall et al. 2017); LZ quotes an older vertical intensity of (5.38 ± 0.07) × 10^-9 cm^-2 s^-1 sr^-1 (Cherry et al. 1983), which is not a flux and is not recorded. Measured at the Davis Campus only; the DUNE far-detector caverns on the same level have no flux measurement.
muon_flux.quote: This rate corresponds to a muon flux of (5.09 ± 0.08stat. ± 0.10sys. ) × 10−9 cm−2 s−1 in the Davis Cavern.

name: Davis Campus, 4850 Level, Sanford Underground Research Facility
notes: The Davis Cavern is the excavation of Raymond Davis Jr.'s chlorine solar-neutrino experiment, begun in the mid-1960s; it was enlarged for dark matter experiments and the Davis Campus opened on 30 May 2012 (SURF, "The Davis Campus").
The Davis Campus hosted LUX (2013-2016) and now hosts LZ; the MAJORANA DEMONSTRATOR occupied the adjacent laboratory space.

summary.plain: A laboratory hall about 1.5 kilometres below the surface in a former gold mine in Lead, South Dakota. It was dug in the 1960s for Ray Davis's experiment that counted neutrinos from the Sun, and it now houses the LZ dark matter detector.
summary.technical: Davis Campus on the 4850 Level of SURF (former Homestake mine), ~1480 m of rock, ~4300 m.w.e. overburden. The enlarged Davis Cavern hosted LUX and now hosts LZ inside the 8 m × 6 m water shield; opened to science 30 May 2012.
